# Bilko Academy

> A free, plain-language course that teaches anyone to use Claude well. 13 short lessons, no coding needed, every claim cited.

Bilko Academy is an independent course, not made or endorsed by Anthropic. It is free and you can read every lesson without an account. Lessons are #/ hash routes inside a JavaScript page, so a plain HTTP fetch of a lesson URL returns only the app shell, not the lesson text.

## Start here

- [Welcome to the Academy](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/intro/welcome): Read this first. Three minutes. (3 min)

## Meet Claude

- [A model, not a search engine](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/meet-claude/a-model-not-a-search-engine): What you're actually talking to when you talk to Claude. (7 min)
- [Tokens and probability — why answers vary](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/meet-claude/tokens-and-probability): Claude reads in chunks and answers with weighted dice. Those two facts explain more than they should. (7 min)
- [The two hard limits — context window and knowledge cutoff](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/meet-claude/the-two-hard-limits): One wall in time, one wall in space — and no prompt can talk Claude past either. (7 min)

## Working in Claude

- [Your first week in claude.ai](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/working-in-claude/your-first-week-in-claude): Four decisions you'll meet in the first week — a plan, a model, two settings, and what Claude remembers. (7 min)
- [Projects — give Claude a standing briefing](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/working-in-claude/projects-a-standing-briefing): Write the context once. Every chat after that starts already briefed. (8 min)
- [Making things — Artifacts, files, and Claude that acts](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/working-in-claude/making-things-artifacts-and-agents): When the answer isn't a paragraph but a document, an app, a report, or a finished job. (7 min)

## Prompting

- [Say what you mean — clarity, context, and roles](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/prompting/say-what-you-mean): Most disappointing answers trace back to a prompt that never said what it wanted. (8 min)
- [Show and structure — examples, XML tags, long documents](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/prompting/show-and-structure): Three techniques, one habit — keep what Claude should read separate from what Claude should do. (7 min)
- [One job per turn — chaining and testing your prompts](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/prompting/one-job-per-turn): Split dependent work into a chain of turns, then prove the new prompt beats the old one. (7 min)

## Trust and next steps

- [Hallucination, trust, and "show me the source"](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/trust-and-next-steps/hallucination-and-when-to-trust): Output is plausible, not verified. Here is the decision rule that handles that. (8 min)
- [Staying safe — prompt injection and the rules of the road](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/trust-and-next-steps/prompt-injection-and-the-rules): When the document Claude is reading tells Claude what to do — and what you actually agreed to when you signed up. (7 min)
- [Claude Code — when chat isn't enough](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/trust-and-next-steps/claude-code-when-chat-isnt-enough): The capstone: an agent that works where your files live. (8 min)

## Optional

- [Glossary](https://bilko.run/projects/academy/#/glossary): Plain-language definitions of the terms used in the lessons.
